findings.claim: the resolve-evidence re-check lived only in the advisory verdict command, not the done gate; nothing automated runs verdict (lanes 1/2/3/7)
symlinked invocation paths made all five tools silent no-ops with exit 0: the entry check compared argv against the realpathed module URL (proven live via /proc/self/cwd)
the no-drift taxonomy self-test was an unfalsifiable identity tautology while PHASE_ORDER and derivePhase stayed local copies in task-coverage and task-workspace
the evidence law was weaker than the RED-check law it claimed to mirror: bare existsSync accepted directories, absolute paths outside the repo, and empty strings
record trusted the live checklist with no exactly-eight pin, so a mid-pass edit widened the recordable lane range; stored registers accepted any lane value
a forged transition to a KNOWN phase still authorizes a workspace; the filter only ignores unknown targets
workspaceSiblingPath still stamps the harness brand when vendored nested, and splits POSIX-only despite the URL-decode fix
findings.justification: nested vendoring is an unsupported layout by WIRING section 1 (tools at the repo root); at root level the derivation names the host repo. Windows is out of scope: the harness depends on POSIX (jj, sh hooks). Noted in issue #2.

findings.claim: the wave's own task record, register, and bundles were untracked at audit time; commit timestamps are neutral by policy while event timestamps are honest session time
findings.justification: records land with the wave they authorize, before any push (established procedure); commit-timestamp neutrality is deliberate policy while event timestamps stay honest — the divergence is the audit trail itself.

findings.claim: no task-to-file tenancy: lane attribution and evidence content remain the client's say-so (bearer citations)
selfTestResolveEvidence could silently skip its assertions when the fixture was refused
banner counts drifted in task-findings and README said four scripts where five exist
findings.justification: bearer citations are the documented plain-JSON trust boundary (issue #8); task-to-file binding and content-bound evidence are registered there as the design work.

findings.claim: git stderr is suppressed in gitOut, trading diagnosability for noise-free gates
findings.justification: stderr suppression in gitOut is deliberate: expected-absent probes (git show of a path missing from an older rev) printed fatal noise during normal operation, and e.message retains the failing command for diagnosis.

findings.claim: register correction: f9 (task-to-file tenancy, bearer citations) was resolved with evidence that does not prove a repair, and f11 (banner drift) received a justification belonging to f9 — f11's actual fix landed in the same wave; corrected here because resolutions are append-only
findings.justification: bearer citations are the documented plain-JSON trust boundary and the registered design work of issue #8; today the gates demand per-commit footers naming a specific valid record, and content-bound evidence is issue #9.
